# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The module diagnoses a SASRec-compatible interface; model internals are not supplied. `view.model` is the trained module, while `view.item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)`, and `predict_score(features, items)` expose embeddings, encoding, and scoring. # Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` reads public training histories from `view.user_train`. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors. Histories are truncated and left-padded to `model.maxlen`. Diagnosis temporarily enables evaluation/inference mode, then restores module modes and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states. When available, `model.predict` must numerically match adapter baseline scores.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding embeddings and reports `(mean pairwise cosine + 1)/2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment, not necessarily collapse; there is no universal good threshold.
- **Training margins:** Across up to ten batches, measures positive-minus-negative logits at valid positions: mean, lower tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative margins indicate stronger sampled training separation.
- **Temporal outcomes:** For up to 50 eligible users, predicts the final training event from its prefix against 99 unique negatives. Reports rank, reciprocal rank, HR@10, sampled top-10 overlap, and changed-minus-baseline differences. Repeats average within users; user bootstrap intervals quantify paired differences.
- **Descriptive controls:** Last-item dot product, normalized history similarity, and training-fitted transition scores provide comparisons. Five independently selected users receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendations per dataset.

# Perturbation & Tests

Tests remove matched amounts of oldest, recent, or random context; delete the final prefix item; shuffle earlier or all events; and substitute unseen items matched approximately by frequency decile. Deletions use packed sequences and, except final-item deletion, zero-filled holes. These reveal intervention sensitivity, but position changes and unverified padding behavior confound recency interpretations.
